transcript.content: Hello. I'm glad you're here today. What brings you in to see me?

I'm here because I've been struggling with a mix of severe depression and some really strange, unsettling experiences for about a year and a half now. It has gotten to the point where I just can't cope on my own anymore.
Could you tell me a bit more about these 'strange, unsettling experiences' you've been having?

It constantly feels like I'm being watched and monitored, even when I'm alone in my own home. I've also been hearing these quiet whispers and voices when there is absolutely no one around. It's just really terrifying and makes me feel so unsafe.
Do you experience these voices and feelings of being watched only when you are feeling deeply depressed, or do they also happen during times when your mood feels relatively normal?

They actually happen even when my mood is relatively stable. There have been times, lasting for a couple of weeks at a stretch, where the deep depression lifted but the voices and the feeling of being watched were still completely there.
Looking back over the last year and a half, would you say you have felt severely depressed for most of that time, or have those depressive feelings only been present for a small part of it?

I've definitely felt severely depressed for the vast majority of the last year and a half. It feels like the heavy, dark cloud has been there almost constantly, with only a few very brief breaks where the sadness lifted slightly.

latest_inference.note: Previously, the candidates were Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type) and Schizophrenia. The patient has now clarified that they have been severely depressed for the vast majority of the 1.5-year duration of their illness. In Schizophrenia, mood episodes must be brief relative to the total duration of the illness, whereas in Schizoaffective Disorder, the mood symptoms must be present for the majority of the illness. Since the depressive symptoms have been present for the vast majority of the time, and they experienced at least a two-week period of psychotic symptoms in the absence of a major mood episode, the diagnosis of Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type) is confirmed, and Schizophrenia is ruled out.
